# v2.54 Release Notes

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.48-dev … v2.54-dev**. The
headline is the new **Compliance Planning** page; it also brings a richer
Dashboard geographic filter, an active/expired Dashboard toggle, and a mobile
menu fix. Features are described in their final, shipped state.

## New: Compliance Planning

Program dashboards tell you **where the gaps are**. Compliance Planning — a new
page under **Programs** — tells you **who to certify, in what order, for the
least effort**, floating the easy wins to the top. It reuses exactly the same
distinct-holder counting — and the same scope rules — as the dashboards, so the
two never disagree.

- **Headline metric: "People to certify".** How many people still need to earn a
  certification to close the plan's gaps, deduplicated so one person whose single
  exam satisfies several requirements counts once.

- **Pick a scope and one or more programs.** Choose Global / Theatre / Region /
  Country, then for each program aim at:
  - a **tier** (the tool picks the cheapest specialisations to get you there), or
    specific specialisation(s), for tiered programs; or
  - specific specialisation(s) or **all requirements**, for flat programs.
  Mixed selections are supported in a single plan (e.g. a tier in one program plus
  all specialisations in another).

- **Scope-consistent with the dashboards.** Each scope plans against **only its
  own-level requirements** — planning one country shows that country's
  requirements, not the theatre-wide requirement above it (select the theatre to
  plan against theatre-level requirements). Gaps are never double-counted.

- **Aggregate roadmap.** Each target shows a plain-language headline ("To reach
  *Gold* in *EMEA*: achieve 1 more specialisation — cheapest are A or B (2 to
  certify each) (achieve any 1). ~2 people to certify.") and a breakdown per
  specialisation and requirement — have / need, the gap, and how many candidates
  sit in each tier. For a tier target, only the cheapest specialisation(s) needed
  to reach the tier are counted, and every equally-cheap alternative is flagged
  **Recommended** so ties aren't hidden.

- **"Who to certify" drill-down.** One row per person listing every gap they close
  (expand for detail), ranked cheapest-first:
  - **Easy win** — did an ILT/OLX that leads to the required cert but never earned
    it; needs only the exam.
  - **Lapsed** — held the cert but it expired; needs only a renewal.
  - **Legacy upgrade** — holds a legacy cert whose replacement is the required one.
  - **Net-new** — needs the full ILT/OLX → cert path; reported as a remaining count.
  Because a person can only be **spent once**, candidates are allocated across the
  whole plan — so someone whose single exam closes the same cert in several places
  appears once, not once per gap.

- **Renewals at risk.** Holders whose qualifying training expires within a
  selectable window (1 / 3 / 6 / 12 months) are surfaced separately — their expiry
  will re-open a gap the plan currently reports as closed.

- **Export.** The candidate list and the renewals list can each be exported to
  CSV, Excel, or PDF.

## Changed: Dashboard

- **Cascading Theatre → Region → Country filter.** The Dashboard's top-right scope
  selector previously filtered by theatre only. It now offers the same cascading
  **Theatre → Region → Country** filter used across the report pages, so you can
  drill the whole dashboard down to a single region or country. Picking a theatre
  limits the region choices; picking a region limits the country choices; changing
  a higher level resets the ones below it. Every metric card and chart updates to
  the selected scope, and previous scopes are cached for instant switching.

- **Active training by default, with an option to include expired.** The metric
  cards and charts count only **active** (non-expired) certifications,
  accreditations, ILTs and OLX by default, so the totals reflect what's currently
  valid. A new **Include expired (inactive)** tickbox next to the geographic
  filter adds expired completions back into every card and chart. Your choice is
  remembered alongside the geographic scope.

## Fixed

- **Mobile menu no longer darkens the page.** Opening the mobile navigation menu
  used to leave a stuck dark band over the phone browser's toolbar areas after
  closing. The menu's background shading has been removed altogether — the
  navigation still slides in and closes by tapping a link, the ✕, or anywhere
  outside, with no dimming and no leftover band, top or bottom.

## Notes

- No database migration and no configuration required for this release.
- Compliance Planning is a live view — it always reflects current data. Saved
  plans and status tracking are planned for a later phase.
